subject.title: Next Sprint B: model-input validation guardrails

question: Should configured model input modalities be constrained to currently runnable chat/media-understanding inputs, preserved as broad provider metadata, or allowed only behind an explicit capability-override contract?
rationale: Current code intentionally accepts and preserves audio/video metadata while runtime and docs still mostly consume text/image semantics, so automation cannot safely choose a stricter contract without breaking existing config expectations.

options.title: Capability-aware guardrail with override
options.body: Preserve broad metadata but reject or warn when a runtime path is about to trust a declared capability that conflicts with known catalog/runtime support, with an explicit override for custom providers.

options.title: Schema clamp to current runtime inputs
options.body: Tighten `models.providers.*.models[].input` to the runtime-supported set and add migration/docs, accepting the compatibility break for existing audio/video metadata.

options.title: Metadata-only contract
options.body: Document audio/video as descriptive metadata and avoid new rejection, leaving runtime-specific diagnostics to narrower follow-up issues.

recommendation.title: Capability-aware guardrail with override
recommendation.body: Preserve broad metadata but reject or warn when a runtime path is about to trust a declared capability that conflicts with known catalog/runtime support, with an explicit override for custom providers.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent is the clearest current routing candidate from recent schema, registry, and release-line history across the affected files.
